objective: Bind the news-vs-no-news drop reversal/drift candidate family (12 preregistered candidates: 2 drop thresholds x 3 hold horizons x 2 legs) to verified source cards and cost-assumption context before the backtest, resolving reports/research/harvest/directions.jsonl's dir:no_news_price_shock_reversal_chan (harvested, never locally tested).

sources.core_claim: Chan (2003), JFE 70(2):223-260: bad-news stocks drift negatively up to 12 months; no-identifiable-news large moves reverse next month; concentrated in small/illiquid stocks, weakens but survives excluding low-priced stocks.
sources.project_applicability: Grounds the event definition (large market-adjusted close-to-close drop) and the news-vs-no-news PIT classification design.
sources.reflection: Abstract-level only (paywalled full text); pre-2000 sample -- the local 2024-2026 backtest is the decisive test of current magnitude, not an assumption that Chan-era numbers transfer.

sources.core_claim: Savor (2012), JFE 106(3):635-659: price shocks with analyst-report coverage drift; shocks without coverage reverse; underreaction to fundamentals, overreaction to non-fundamental shocks.
sources.project_applicability: Second, methodologically distinct source (analyst reports vs. headlines) behind the same mechanism; supports both the long no-news leg and the short news-drift leg.
sources.reflection: Abstract-level only; SSRN/ScienceDirect both 403 on WebFetch this pass.

sources.core_claim: Dyl, Yuksel & Zaynutdinova (2019), Journal of Business Research 95:1-12: independent replication through 2015 of the same overreaction/underreaction pattern; effect larger in small/low-institutional-ownership firms; magnitude of BOTH reversals and continuations declined after post-decimalization liquidity improvements.
sources.project_applicability: Newest (2015-sample) independent replication located; its decay finding sets an honest prior against assuming Chan-era magnitudes hold in the far more liquid, more algorithmic 2024-2026 window.
sources.reflection: Abstract-level synthesis via WebSearch only (ScienceDirect/SSRN 403); no post-2020 independent replication of this mechanism was found in 4 targeted WebSearch queries this pass.

sources.core_claim: Broker-published stock borrow fee schedule: easy-to-borrow US equities commonly carry annualized borrow fees from roughly 0.25% up to a few percent, materially below hard-to-borrow names (which can exceed 30-100%/yr).
sources.project_applicability: Supports the brief's preregistered 1%/year borrow-fee assumption for the short news-drift leg (restricted to the top-1000-ADV, easy-to-borrow-proxy tier) as a plausible, slightly conservative (not favorable) rate, not a number invented for this iteration.
sources.reflection: Current broker fee schedule, not a historical time series over the TEST window; used only for plausibility context, the brief's 1%/yr figure is used as-is (a frozen, preregistered assumption, not tuned to this source).

sources.core_claim: Borrow fees are quoted as annualized rates but assessed daily; for the large majority of liquid, easy-to-borrow US equities, fees cluster well under 1%/yr, with sharp increases only for names that become hard-to-borrow (float scarcity, high short demand).
sources.project_applicability: Further corroborates the plausibility of the brief's 1%/yr borrow-cost assumption and the top-1000-ADV easy-to-borrow-proxy restriction on the short leg.
sources.reflection: Practitioner blog, not peer-reviewed; used for cost-plausibility context only, does not change the preregistered contract.

sources.core_claim: Bid-ask spread costs rise sharply with declining liquidity: large-cap S&P 500 names trade near single-digit basis points round-trip, while small-cap/illiquid names can cost 50+ bp round trip or 1-2%/yr in aggregate spread cost for a small-cap strategy.
sources.project_applicability: Supports the plausibility of the brief's preregistered ADV-tiered spread schedule (top-500 3bp, 500-1000 6bp, 1000-1500 12bp per side) as directionally consistent with published liquidity-cost gradients, not a number invented for this iteration.
sources.reflection: General-audience explainer, not a primary transaction-cost study; used for plausibility context only -- the brief's own tiered cost table is applied as-is, a frozen preregistered assumption.

sources.core_claim: Two placebos preregistered per the brief: (i) news/no-news labels shuffled across that day's qualifying events (trade-level, same drop set, relabeled); (ii) the same stocks redated to random non-event trading dates within the sample. Both are computed at the trade level (average return per trade, t-stat clustered by date), not as separate full portfolio books.
sources.project_applicability: Falsification design for all 12 candidates; establishes whether the news/no-news label itself (not just 'a large drop happened') carries the return difference.
sources.reflection: Not an external source; required by the brief's own preregistered decision rule (trade-level edge over the shuffled-label placebo, t>=2).

sources.core_claim: Liquidity tiering reuses the existing project-wide PIT ADV rank (data/features/universe_broad: 60-trading-day trailing dollar-ADV window, ranked and snapped at each completed month-end, held constant until the next month-end) rather than building a new literal 21-day-at-t-1 rolling ranker -- the same tiering convention already used by signal_card.py's TIER_EDGES and other 2026-09-29 iterations (e.g. T-20260929-01). Both PIT news classification sources (data/features/news_packets headlines, data/features/earnings_events 8-K item-2.02 filings) have dense coverage starting only in 2024, which is why the brief's STRESS window (2016-2023) is documented as data-infeasible for this mechanism and TEST (2024-2026) is used as the sole decisive window.
sources.project_applicability: Documents two deliberate, disclosed deviations from the brief's literal data spec (ADV window length, STRESS-window infeasibility) made for reuse-first and PIT-correctness reasons, not to help any candidate pass.
sources.reflection: Internal engineering/data-coverage note, not an external claim; the underlying coverage counts were measured directly from the local parquet files this session (see data-feasibility.json).
